evidence: The solutions all directly enumerate triangle witnesses: "if c in adj[b]", "look for a node w", and "candidates b > a with edge a-b".
affordance_in_statement: It is guaranteed that the reaction registry contains at least one set of three chemicals that pairwise react. Any such set proves two units cannot suffice. Output one such set.
removal_suggestion: There is no safe removal or rewording that preserves the required output for every input: the existence of a valid triangle is the core feasibility premise. It can only be presented indirectly, such as by describing the registry as an instance known to admit a three-chemical impossibility certificate.

recommended_edit: No task-preserving edit can reliably defeat all survivors; any edit removing the guaranteed triangle would make the mandated three-integer output potentially invalid. If presentation must change, replace the explicit guarantee with an indirect statement that the selected registry is known to make two-unit allocation impossible while retaining the same valid-output promise.
